title: Why You See Moving Dots After Staring at Bright Colours
hook: Your brain creates moving dots after you stare at bright colours.

narration.text: Stare at a bright colour for a moment, then look away at a plain surface.
You will see a ghostly afterimage, sometimes with moving patterns.
This happens because your eye's colour sensors get tired.
The fatigued sensors send weaker signals to your brain.
Your brain then overcompensates, making you see the opposite colours.
It is a normal effect, and you can test it with any colourful image.
Try it right now and tell me if it worked on you, like this if it surprised you, and subscribe for more brain insights.

description: Have you ever stared at a bright colour and then looked away to see a strange afterimage or moving dots? This video explains the fascinating reason behind this common visual phenomenon. It is all about how your eye's colour sensors respond to strong stimuli.
topic: Why you sometimes see moving dots or patterns after staring at a strong colour. You can test this right now with a colourful image.
